$comment: Architecture boundaries for the Apps Script layer. Each rule is a *claim about the code* that a script can check. Keep rules few and true: a rule that has to be explained away in a comment is a rule we do not have. Edit here, not in the checker.

layers.pure: No Google service, no clock, no random, no logging side effect: input -> output only.
layers.coordinator: Orchestrates a command: lock, policy, services, persist, audit. Named '<verb>Request' or listed in coordinators.
layers.boundary: Owns a service handle (Sheets/Calendar/Properties/Cache/Lock/UrlFetch) and nothing else.

rules.title: the booking path never calls a model
rules.why: A booking must never depend on Gemini, Groq or any provider. The assistant is administrative only.

rules.title: a pure function stays pure
rules.why: A validator that reads Properties or the clock cannot be tested in isolation, and its result stops being a function of its input.

notYetPure.validateRequest_: reads visit types through clinicServices_() and compares against the clock, so it cannot be tested without a property store — extracting readVisitServices_ from the validator is a separate, reviewed change
notYetPure.isValidDay_: parses through `new Date('T12:00:00')`; it is pure in effect (no clock read) but not pure in shape, and the gate does not get to assume that
notYetPure.clinicWeekday_: no clock read (Date.UTC on a literal), same shape problem as isValidDay_ — the call is deterministic, the scan cannot see it
notYetPure.retentionCutoff_: reads the clock by design; it belongs to the coordinator layer, not the pure layer
notYetPure.visitDuration_: resolves the duration from Script Properties; duration is policy, so this is a boundary function wearing a domain name

rules.scope: functions-only, because Code.gs legitimately owns the Google services in its boundary functions

rules.title: every mutation takes the script lock before it writes
rules.why: LockService is the only thing preventing two approvals from consuming the same slot. Apps Script has no transaction to fall back on.

rules.title: a command answers through the response contract
rules.why: app.js switches on ok/message/reference/booking. A coordinator that returns a bare boolean or throws breaks the caller silently.

rules.title: no secret literal in the application sources
rules.why: Secrets live in Script Properties. A literal is a leak that outlives the incident.

statusVocabulary.why: One list, used by the checker and the document. A status that appears only inside a coordinator guard is an unwritten rule.
